sentences.text: This animal belonged to the Ziphosuchia group, a branch of notosuchian crocodyliforms.
Its lower jaw featured a distinct Y-shaped outline and unique teeth positioned on the inner side of the front bone.
The front pair of teeth stood out because they were larger and pointed forward, while the entire skull fragment measured just 70.5 millimeters long.
The entire known skeleton is tiny, measuring only 70.5 millimeters in length.
The Y-shaped jaw and small inner teeth are bizarre features not seen in other relatives.
Scientists named this genus in 2011 after finding fossils at the Serra do Veadinho site within the Serra da Galga Formation.
The single known specimen, cataloged as DGM 1480-R, earned a name combining Greek words for forceps and crocodile, while the species name honors the local community.
This creature lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Experts cannot yet determine its exact diet or precise evolutionary position because the fossil record is incomplete.
